# zla_herfsx_extended

> Extra-precise iterative refinement for Hermitian indefinite linear systems.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlaHerfsxExtended from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zla_herfsx_extended';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zla_herfsx_extended(
    order,
    prec_type,
    uplo,
    N, nrhs,
    A, LDA,
    AF, LDAF,
    IPIV, strideIPIV,
    colequ,
    c, strideC,
    B, LDB,
    Y, LDY,
    BERR_OUT, strideBERR_OUT,
    n_norms,
    ERR_BNDS_NORM, LDERR_BNDS_NORM,
    ERR_BNDS_COMP, LDERR_BNDS_COMP,
    RES, strideRES,
    AYB, strideAYB,
    DY, strideDY,
    Y_TAIL, strideY_TAIL,
    rcond, ithresh, rthresh, dz_ub, ignore_cwise
) → integer
```

Improves the computed solution using extra-precise iterative refinement for Hermitian indefinite matrices.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `prec_type` | `integer` | Requested residual precision (ignored; see base.js) |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix `A`<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of right-hand sides<br>Requires `nrhs ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Original Hermitian matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `AF` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Factored form of `A` |
| ↳ `LDAF` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `AF`<br>Requires `LDAF ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Pivot indices |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | Stride length for `IPIV` |
| `colequ` | `boolean` | Whether column equilibration was performed on `A` |
| `c` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Column scale factors |
| ↳ `strideC` | `integer` | Stride length for `c` |
| `B` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | Right-hand side matrix |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `B`<br>Column-major requires `LDB ≥ max(1, N)`<br>Row-major requires `LDB ≥ max(1, nrhs)` |
| `Y` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | **in/out** · Initial/improved solution |
| ↳ `LDY` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Y`<br>Column-major requires `LDY ≥ max(1, N)`<br>Row-major requires `LDY ≥ max(1, nrhs)` |
| `BERR_OUT` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nrhs</sub> | **out** · Componentwise backward error |
| ↳ `strideBERR_OUT` | `integer` | Stride length for `berrOut` |
| `n_norms` | `integer` | Number of error bound components |
| `ERR_BNDS_NORM` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>nrhs × N_ERR_BNDS</sub> | **in/out** · Normwise error bounds |
| ↳ `LDERR_BNDS_NORM` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `errBndsNorm` |
| `ERR_BNDS_COMP` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>nrhs × N_ERR_BNDS</sub> | **in/out** · Componentwise error bounds |
| ↳ `LDERR_BNDS_COMP` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `errBndsComp` |
| `RES` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Workspace residual |
| ↳ `strideRES` | `integer` | Stride length for `RES` |
| `AYB` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Real workspace |
| ↳ `strideAYB` | `integer` | Stride length for `AYB` |
| `DY` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Correction workspace |
| ↳ `strideDY` | `integer` | Stride length for `DY` |
| `Y_TAIL` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Double-double tail of `Y` |
| ↳ `strideY_TAIL` | `integer` | Stride length for `yTail` |
| `rcond` | `number` | Reciprocal condition number |
| `ithresh` | `integer` | Maximum refinement iterations |
| `rthresh` | `number` | Convergence ratio threshold |
| `dz_ub` | `number` | Componentwise update upper bound |
| `ignore_cwise` | `boolean` | Whether to ignore componentwise convergence |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `prec_type`: Specifies the intermediate precision to be used in refinement. The value is defined by ILAPREC(P) where P is a CHARACTER and P

  -   = 'S': Single
  -   = 'D': Double
  -   = 'I': Indigenous
  -   = 'X' or 'E': Extra
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The number of linear equations, i.e., the order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right-hand-sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B.
- `A`: On entry, the N-by-N matrix A.
- `AF`: The block diagonal matrix D and the multipliers used to obtain the factor U or L as computed by ZHETRF.
- `IPIV`: Details of the interchanges and the block structure of D as determined by ZHETRF.
- `colequ`: If .TRUE. then column equilibration was done to A before calling this routine. This is needed to compute the solution and error bounds correctly.
- `c`: The column scale factors for A. If `COLEQU` = .FALSE., C is not accessed. If C is input, each element of C should be a power of the radix to ensure a reliable solution and error estimates. Scaling by powers of the radix does not cause rounding errors unless the result underflows or overflows. Rounding errors during scaling lead to refining with a matrix that is not equivalent to the input matrix, producing error estimates that may not be reliable.
- `B`: The right-hand-side matrix B.
- `Y`: On entry, the solution matrix X, as computed by ZHETRS. On exit, the improved solution matrix Y.
- `BERR_OUT`: On exit, `BERR_OUT(j)` contains the componentwise relative backward error for right-hand-side j from the formula

  $$
  \max (i) ( \lvert \mathrm{RES}(i) \rvert / ( \lvert \operatorname{op}(\mathrm{A\_s}) \rvert \, \lvert Y \rvert + \lvert \mathrm{B\_s} \rvert )(i) )
  $$

  where abs(Z) is the componentwise absolute value of the matrix or vector Z. This is computed by ZLA\_LIN\_BERR.
- `n_norms`: Determines which error bounds to return (see `ERR_BNDS_NORM` and `ERR_BNDS_COMP`). If $\mathrm{N\_NORMS} \ge 1$ return normwise error bounds. If $\mathrm{N\_NORMS} \ge 2$ return componentwise error bounds.
- `ERR_BNDS_NORM`: For each right-hand side, this array contains information about various error bounds and condition numbers corresponding to the normwise relative error, which is defined as follows:

  Normwise relative error in the ith solution vector:

  max\_j (abs(XTRUE(j,i) - X(j,i))) ------------------------------ max\_j abs(X(j,i))

  The array is indexed by the type of error information as described below. There currently are up to three pieces of information returned.

  The first index in `ERR_BNDS_NORM(i,:)` corresponds to the ith right-hand side.

  The second index in `ERR_BNDS_NORM(:,err)` contains the following three fields: err = 1 "Trust/don't trust" boolean. Trust the answer if the

  -   reciprocal condition number is less than the threshold
  -   sqrt(n) \* slamch('Epsilon').

  err = 2 "Guaranteed" error bound: The estimated forward error,

  -   almost certainly within a factor of 10 of the true error
  -   so long as the next entry is greater than the threshold
  -   sqrt(n) \* slamch('Epsilon'). This error bound should only
  -   be trusted if the previous boolean is true.

  err = 3 Reciprocal condition number: Estimated normwise

  -   reciprocal condition number. Compared with the threshold
  -   sqrt(n) \* slamch('Epsilon') to determine if the error
  -   estimate is "guaranteed". These reciprocal condition
  -   numbers are 1 / (norm(Z^{-1},inf) \* norm(Z,inf)) for some
  -   appropriately scaled matrix Z.
  -   Let $Z = S \, A$, where S scales each row by a power of the
  -   radix so all absolute row sums of Z are approximately 1.

  This subroutine is only responsible for setting the second field above. See Lapack Working Note 165 for further details and extra cautions.
- `ERR_BNDS_COMP`: For each right-hand side, this array contains information about various error bounds and condition numbers corresponding to the componentwise relative error, which is defined as follows:

  Componentwise relative error in the ith solution vector:

  abs(XTRUE(j,i) - X(j,i)) max\_j ---------------------- abs(X(j,i))

  The array is indexed by the right-hand side i (on which the componentwise relative error depends), and the type of error information as described below. There currently are up to three pieces of information returned for each right-hand side. If componentwise accuracy is not requested (PARAMS(3) = 0.0), then `ERR_BNDS_COMP` is not accessed. If $\mathrm{N\_ERR\_BNDS} < 3$, then at most the first (:,N\_ERR\_BNDS) entries are returned.

  The first index in `ERR_BNDS_COMP(i,:)` corresponds to the ith right-hand side.

  The second index in `ERR_BNDS_COMP(:,err)` contains the following three fields: err = 1 "Trust/don't trust" boolean. Trust the answer if the

  -   reciprocal condition number is less than the threshold
  -   sqrt(n) \* slamch('Epsilon').

  err = 2 "Guaranteed" error bound: The estimated forward error,

  -   almost certainly within a factor of 10 of the true error
  -   so long as the next entry is greater than the threshold
  -   sqrt(n) \* slamch('Epsilon'). This error bound should only
  -   be trusted if the previous boolean is true.

  err = 3 Reciprocal condition number: Estimated componentwise

  -   reciprocal condition number. Compared with the threshold
  -   sqrt(n) \* slamch('Epsilon') to determine if the error
  -   estimate is "guaranteed". These reciprocal condition
  -   numbers are 1 / (norm(Z^{-1},inf) \* norm(Z,inf)) for some
  -   appropriately scaled matrix Z.
  -   Let $Z = S \, (A \, \operatorname{diag}(x))$, where x is the solution for the
  -   current right-hand side and S scales each row of
  -   $A \, \operatorname{diag}(x)$ by a power of the radix so all absolute row
  -   sums of Z are approximately 1.

  This subroutine is only responsible for setting the second field above. See Lapack Working Note 165 for further details and extra cautions.
- `RES`: Workspace to hold the intermediate residual.
- `AYB`: Workspace.
- `DY`: Workspace to hold the intermediate solution.
- `Y_TAIL`: Workspace to hold the trailing bits of the intermediate solution.
- `rcond`: Reciprocal scaled condition number. This is an estimate of the reciprocal Skeel condition number of the matrix A after equilibration (if done). If this is less than the machine precision (in particular, if it is zero), the matrix is singular to working precision. Note that the error may still be small even if this number is very small and the matrix appears ill- conditioned.
- `ithresh`: The maximum number of residual computations allowed for refinement. The default is 10. For 'aggressive' set to 100 to permit convergence using approximate factorizations or factorizations other than LU. If the factorization uses a technique other than Gaussian elimination, the guarantees in `ERR_BNDS_NORM` and `ERR_BNDS_COMP` may no longer be trustworthy.
- `rthresh`: Determines when to stop refinement if the error estimate stops decreasing. Refinement will stop when the next solution no longer satisfies norm(dx\_{i+1}) \< `RTHRESH` \* norm(dx\_i) where norm(Z) is the infinity norm of Z. `RTHRESH` satisfies $0 < \mathrm{RTHRESH} \le 1$. The default value is 0.5. For 'aggressive' set to 0.9 to permit convergence on extremely ill-conditioned matrices. See LAWN 165 for more details.
- `dz_ub`: Determines when to start considering componentwise convergence. Componentwise convergence is only considered after each component of the solution Y is stable, which we define as the relative change in each component being less than `DZ_UB`. The default value is 0.25, requiring the first bit to be stable. See LAWN 165 for more details.
- `ignore_cwise`: If .TRUE. then ignore componentwise convergence. Default value is .FALSE..

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (`0` on success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` sixteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` sixteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` eighteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` eighteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zla_herfsx_extended.ndarray(
    prec_type,
    uplo,
    N, nrhs,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    AF, strideAF1, strideAF2, offsetAF,
    IPIV, strideIPIV, offsetIPIV,
    colequ,
    c, strideC, offsetC,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    Y, strideY1, strideY2, offsetY,
    BERR_OUT, strideBERR_OUT, offsetBERR_OUT,
    n_norms,
    ERR_BNDS_NORM, strideERR_BNDS_NORM1, strideERR_BNDS_NORM2, offsetERR_BNDS_NORM,
    ERR_BNDS_COMP, strideERR_BNDS_COMP1, strideERR_BNDS_COMP2, offsetERR_BNDS_COMP,
    RES, strideRES, offsetRES,
    AYB, strideAYB, offsetAYB,
    DY, strideDY, offsetDY,
    Y_TAIL, strideY_TAIL, offsetY_TAIL,
    rcond, ithresh, rthresh, dz_ub, ignore_cwise
) → integer
```

Improves the computed solution using extra-precise iterative refinement for Hermitian indefinite matrices.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `prec_type` | `integer` | Requested residual precision (currently ignored; see base.js) |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix `A`<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of right-hand sides<br>Requires `nrhs ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Original Hermitian matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` |
| `AF` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Factored form of `A` |
| ↳ `strideAF1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `AF` |
| ↳ `strideAF2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `AF` |
| ↳ `offsetAF` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `AF` |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Pivot indices from `zhetrf` |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | Stride length for `IPIV` |
| ↳ `offsetIPIV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `IPIV` |
| `colequ` | `boolean` | Whether column equilibration was performed on `A` |
| `c` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Column scale factors for `A` |
| ↳ `strideC` | `integer` | Stride length for `c` |
| ↳ `offsetC` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `c` |
| `B` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | Right-hand side matrix |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `B` |
| `Y` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | **in/out** · Initial/improved solution |
| ↳ `strideY1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `Y` |
| ↳ `strideY2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `Y` |
| ↳ `offsetY` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `Y` |
| `BERR_OUT` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nrhs</sub> | **out** · Componentwise backward error |
| ↳ `strideBERR_OUT` | `integer` | Stride length for `berrOut` |
| ↳ `offsetBERR_OUT` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `berrOut` |
| `n_norms` | `integer` | Number of error bound components |
| `ERR_BNDS_NORM` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>nrhs × N_ERR_BNDS</sub> | **in/out** · Normwise error bounds |
| ↳ `strideERR_BNDS_NORM1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `errBndsNorm` |
| ↳ `strideERR_BNDS_NORM2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `errBndsNorm` |
| ↳ `offsetERR_BNDS_NORM` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `errBndsNorm` |
| `ERR_BNDS_COMP` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>nrhs × N_ERR_BNDS</sub> | **in/out** · Componentwise error bounds |
| ↳ `strideERR_BNDS_COMP1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `errBndsComp` |
| ↳ `strideERR_BNDS_COMP2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `errBndsComp` |
| ↳ `offsetERR_BNDS_COMP` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `errBndsComp` |
| `RES` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Workspace residual |
| ↳ `strideRES` | `integer` | Stride length for `RES` |
| ↳ `offsetRES` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `RES` |
| `AYB` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Real workspace |
| ↳ `strideAYB` | `integer` | Stride length for `AYB` |
| ↳ `offsetAYB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `AYB` |
| `DY` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Complex correction workspace |

| `rcond` | `number` | Reciprocal condition number |
| `ithresh` | `integer` | Maximum refinement iterations |
| `rthresh` | `number` | Convergence ratio threshold |
| `dz_ub` | `number` | Componentwise update upper bound |
| `ignore_cwise` | `boolean` | Whether to ignore componentwise convergence |

- `ithresh`: The maximum number of residual computations allowed for refinement. The default is 10. For 'aggressive' set to 100 to permit convergence using approximate factorizations or factorizations other than LU. If the factorization uses a technique other than Gaussian elimination, the guarantees in `ERR_BNDS_NORM` and `ERR_BNDS_COMP` may no longer be trustworthy.
- `rthresh`: Determines when to stop refinement if the error estimate stops decreasing. Refinement will stop when the next solution no longer satisfies norm(dx\_{i+1}) \< `RTHRESH` \* norm(dx\_i) where norm(Z) is the infinity norm of Z. `RTHRESH` satisfies $0 < \mathrm{RTHRESH} \le 1$. The default value is 0.5. For 'aggressive' set to 0.9 to permit convergence on extremely ill-conditioned matrices. See LAWN 165 for more details.
- `dz_ub`: Determines when to start considering componentwise convergence. Componentwise convergence is only considered after each component of the solution Y is stable, which we define as the relative change in each component being less than `DZ_UB`. The default value is 0.25, requiring the first bit to be stable. See LAWN 165 for more details.
- `ignore_cwise`: If .TRUE. then ignore componentwise convergence. Default value is .FALSE..

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (`0` on success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `TypeError` `N` must be a nonnegative integer
- `TypeError` `nrhs` must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: Successful exit.
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the ith argument to ZLA\_HERFSX\_EXTENDED had an illegal value

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zla_herfsx_extended()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZLA_HERFSX_EXTENDED`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zla_herfsx_extended.f).
-   This routine improves the computed solution `Y` to a Hermitian indefinite system `A*X = B` and returns per-right-hand-side backward and forward error bounds.
-   Extended-precision BLAS calls (`BLAS_ZHEMV_X`, `BLAS_ZHEMV2_X`) from the Fortran reference are substituted with plain `zhemv`, since double-double extended-precision BLAS is not available in the runtime. The `precType` argument is accepted but currently has no effect on residual precision.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import zlaHerfsxExtended from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zla_herfsx_extended';

// Construct a 2x2 Hermitian matrix A (column-major).
const A = new Complex128Array( 4 );
const Av = new Float64Array( A.buffer );
const AF = new Complex128Array( 4 );
const AFv = new Float64Array( AF.buffer );
const IPIV = new Int32Array( [ 0, 1 ] );
const c = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 1.0 ] );
const B = new Complex128Array( 2 );
const Bv = new Float64Array( B.buffer );
const Y = new Complex128Array( 2 );
const berrOut = new Float64Array( 1 );
const errBndsNorm = new Float64Array( 3 );
const errBndsComp = new Float64Array( 3 );
const RES = new Complex128Array( 2 );
const AYB = new Float64Array( 2 );
const DY = new Complex128Array( 2 );
const yTail = new Complex128Array( 2 );

Av[ 0 ] = 4.0;
Av[ 2 ] = 1.0;
Av[ 3 ] = 1.0;
Av[ 4 ] = 1.0;
Av[ 5 ] = -1.0;
Av[ 6 ] = 3.0;
AFv.set( Av );
Bv[ 0 ] = 1.0;
Bv[ 2 ] = 2.0;

zlaHerfsxExtended.ndarray( 1, 'upper', 2, 1, A, 1, 2, 0, AF, 1, 2, 0, IPIV, 1, 0, false, c, 1, 0, B, 1, 2, 0, Y, 1, 2, 0, berrOut, 1, 0, 2, errBndsNorm, 1, 1, 0, errBndsComp, 1, 1, 0, RES, 1, 0, AYB, 1, 0, DY, 1, 0, yTail, 1, 0, 1e-10, 10, 0.5, 0.25, false );
console.log( berrOut ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLA_HERFSX_EXTENDED`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLA\_HERFSX\_EXTENDED improves the computed solution to a system of linear equations by performing extra-precise iterative refinement and provides error bounds and backward error estimates for the solution. This subroutine is called by ZHERFSX to perform iterative refinement. In addition to normwise error bound, the code provides maximum componentwise error bound if possible. See comments for `ERR_BNDS_NORM` and `ERR_BNDS_COMP` for details of the error bounds. Note that this subroutine is only responsible for setting the second fields of `ERR_BNDS_NORM` and `ERR_BNDS_COMP`.

</section>
